Required findings: Patient has a diagnosis of prostate cancer.
Patient is considered high risk for recurrence or metastasis based on clinical and pathological factors (e.g., Gleason score, PSA level, time since radical prostatectomy).
Patient has experienced biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy.
Patient has a life expectancy of at least 10 years.
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > Prolaris > Test information (TOC: S3.58.3)

Non-Indications: Patients with low or favorable intermediate disease risk.
Patients with unfavorable intermediate- and high-risk disease who do not meet the life expectancy criteria.
Patients who have not undergone radical prostatectomy.
Patients who have not experienced biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy.
Important criteria & exceptions: Prolaris is considered Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven.
The test requires tissue obtained from either prostate biopsy or surgically removed tissue.
The Prolaris score must be combined with the patient's Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment (CAPRA) score to generate the 10-year prostate cancer-specific mortality risk.
Documentation required: Patient medical record documenting diagnosis of prostate cancer.
Pathology report from prostate biopsy or surgically removed tissue.
Clinical notes detailing patient's risk factors (e.g., Gleason score, PSA level).
Clinical notes detailing time since radical prostatectomy and biochemical recurrence status.
Patient's Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment (CAPRA) score documentation.
